rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding interstitial carbon (0.1–0.5 wt%) to promote carbide precipitates, while the target paper added 4.2 at.% Cr to form a Laves phase. These are different kinds of interventions (interstitial doping vs. substitutional alloying), so they do not match.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature creep testing at 800–1000°C, whereas the target paper performed room-temperature compression testing. These are contradictory regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis relies on nanoscale carbide precipitation strengthening for creep resistance, while the target paper describes a dual mechanism of solid solution hardening and crack hindrance from a reticulated Laves phase. These are different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved high-temperature creep resistance with preserved room-temperature properties, while the target paper reports concurrent increases in room-temperature yield strength and fracture strain. The predicted property (creep resistance) and temperature regime differ from the target's outcome.
